page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-32-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 processor architecture. It offers 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 252 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This hardware configuration does not feature graphical processing units.

The defining characteristic of this configuration is its integrated direct-attached storage tier, consisting of four local NVMe solid-state drives delivering 15,032 GB of aggregate local storage. This local NVMe setup delivers high-throughput and low-latency storage access directly from the host hardware, bypassing network overhead associated with remote block storage volumes. The server provision does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In qualitative terms, cost efficiency is realized through the tight pairing of substantial memory with high-density local NVMe capacity on a single 32-core node. By consolidating more than 15 TB of high-speed storage within the instance boundary, data pipelines avoid external storage egress or remote volume provision expenses. The operational tradeoff is that direct-attached NVMe storage is ephemeral, requiring resilient architectural design and application-layer data replication to safeguard state.

The z4d-highmem-32-highlssd instance is engineered primarily for storage-bound and memory-intensive applications. It is appropriate for distributed NoSQL databases, high-throughput transactional databases, large-scale caching layers, and real-time big data processing workloads requiring massive local disk scratch space.
